activity_context.topic_title: Double Integrals Over Type I Regions

feedback.problem: If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y=3-{x}^{2}$ and $y=x+1,$ then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's make a sketch of our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14054607/assets/7316d667d7308ac5ec0f5348055d3d0e7eb90b97abaa74f5693c3151dc3b8bb1.png)

Now, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. 

- To determine the $x$-limits, we need to find the $x$-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3-{x}^{2} & =x+1 \\ {x}^{2}+x-2 & =0 \\ (x-1)(x+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x$-limits are 
$-2\le x\le 1.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14054607/assets/aab6fb99694b518bfa9d200a75876c9e888ba1ab7d699464bc9caca360be775a.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 1,\,x+1\le y\le 3-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}{\int }_{x+1}^{3-{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\text{ }dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{1}[{\int }_{x+1}^{3-{x}^{2}}f(x,y)\text{ }dy]dx\end{aligned}
$$
